validated_results.title: A Common Variant in the SETD7 Gene Predicts Serum Lycopene Concentrations.
validated_results.reason: This genome-wide association study evaluates genetic variants (SETD7, SCARB1) as predictors of serum lycopene concentrations and reports no population-wide lycopene-prostate cancer incidence estimate.

validated_results.title: Associations between fruit, vegetable and legume intakes and prostate cancer risk: results from the prospective Supplémentation en Vitamines et Minéraux Antioxydants (SU.VI.MAX) cohort.
validated_results.reason: Prospective SU.VI.MAX cohort reporting a hazard ratio for legume intake tertiles and incident prostate cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: Highest vs lowest tertile of legume intake
extraction.timing: Prospective dietary assessment during first 2 years of follow-up (1994-2007)
extraction.population: Male participants of the SU.VI.MAX cohort completing at least three 24-h dietary records

sample_size.excerpt: This study included 3313 male participants to the SUpplémentation en VItamines et Minéraux AntioXydants cohort (follow-up: 1994-2007) who completed at least three 24-h dietary records during the first 2 years of follow-up.

cases.excerpt: After a median follow-up of 12·6 years, 139 incident prostate cancers were diagnosed.

effect_size.excerpt: An inverse association was observed between prostate cancer risk and tertiles of legume intake (hazard ratio (HR)T3v.T1=0·53; 95 % CI 0·34, 0·85; P trend=0·009).

confidence_interval.excerpt: An inverse association was observed between prostate cancer risk and tertiles of legume intake (hazard ratio (HR)T3v.T1=0·53; 95 % CI 0·34, 0·85; P trend=0·009).

design.excerpt: Associations between tertiles of intake and prostate cancer risk were assessed by multivariate Cox proportional hazards models.

timing.excerpt: who completed at least three 24-h dietary records during the first 2 years of follow-up
